## Code Review Best Practices

**Before Review:**
- Keep pull requests small and focused (under 400 lines when possible)
- Write clear, descriptive commit messages and PR descriptions
- Include context about what changed and why
- Self-review your code first to catch obvious issues

**During Review:**
- Focus on logic, architecture, and maintainability over style
- Look for security vulnerabilities and performance issues
- Check for proper error handling and edge cases
- Verify tests cover new functionality adequately
- Ensure code follows team conventions and standards

**Reviewer Guidelines:**
- Provide constructive, specific feedback with examples
- Ask questions rather than make demands when uncertain
- Acknowledge good practices and improvements
- Be timely - review within 24-48 hours when possible
- Use automated tools for style/formatting issues

**Team Process:**
- Establish clear review criteria and checklists
- Require at least one approval before merging
- Use pair programming for complex features
- Document decisions and patterns for future reference
- Foster a learning culture, not a gatekeeping one

**Tools & Automation:**
- Use linters, formatters, and static analysis tools
- Implement CI/CD pipelines with automated testing
- Set up branch protection rules
- Use review templates for consistency
